title: Spiral Matrix
oneLinerQuestion: Return all elements of an m x n matrix in spiral order.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Spiral Matrix problem asks us to return all elements of an M x N matrix in spiral order, starting from the top-left corner and traversing clockwise. Traversing inward in spiral layers requires systematically sweeping the perimeter of the current matrix area and then contracting the active boundaries inward. By maintaining four boundary pointers (top, bottom, left, right), we can trace each layer predictably without needing an extra 2D visited array.

- Step 1: Boundary Variable Initialization — We initialize four boundaries corresponding to the active perimeter: 'top = 0', 'bottom = matrix.length - 1', 'left = 0', and 'right = matrix[0].length - 1'. We also initialize an array 'result = []' to accumulate elements in order.

- Step 2: Spiral Traversal Loop — The algorithm continues inside a while loop as long as the horizontal and vertical bounds remain valid: (top <= bottom && left <= right).

- Step 3: Directional Layer Sweeps — Each cycle executes four distinct edge sweeps in order: (1) Traverse Left to Right across row 'top' from 'left' to 'right', then contract top boundary with 'top++'. (2) Traverse Top to Bottom down column 'right' from 'top' to 'bottom', then contract right boundary with 'right--'. (3) Traverse Right to Left across row 'bottom' from 'right' to 'left' (guarded by if (top <= bottom)), then contract bottom boundary with 'bottom--'. (4) Traverse Bottom to Top up column 'left' from 'bottom' to 'top' (guarded by if (left <= right)), then contract left boundary with 'left++'.

- Step 4: Guarding Single Row or Column Overlaps — The inner condition checks (top <= bottom and left <= right) before executing the bottom and left sweeps prevent double-visiting rows or columns in non-square matrices where boundaries meet prematurely.

- Step 5: Termination & Output — When the boundaries cross each other, every element has been visited exactly once, and 'result' contains all elements in clockwise spiral order.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(M * N) because every element in the M x N matrix is visited exactly once. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space (excluding the output array) since boundary indices manage the traversal directly.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION spiralOrder(matrix):
    top = 0, bottom = LENGTH(matrix) - 1, left = 0, right = LENGTH(matrix[0]) - 1, res = []
    WHILE top <= bottom AND left <= right DO:
        FOR i FROM left TO right DO APPEND matrix[top][i] TO res
        top = top + 1
        FOR i FROM top TO bottom DO APPEND matrix[i][right] TO res
        right = right - 1
        IF top <= bottom THEN
            FOR i FROM right DOWN TO left DO APPEND matrix[bottom][i] TO res
            bottom = bottom - 1
        END IF
        IF left <= right THEN
            FOR i FROM bottom DOWN TO top DO APPEND matrix[i][left] TO res
            left = left + 1
        END IF
    END WHILE
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
